newsitem.title: USA: Tidewater to trim debt before another deal.
newsitem.headline: Tidewater to trim debt before another deal.

text.p: Tidewater Inc will pay down debt from its soon-to-be completed $525 million O.I.L. Ltd deal before shopping for another acquisition to expand its offshore marine operations, Chairman Bill O'Malley said on Wednesday.

The New Orleans-based company expects its latest acquisition to close by May 20 when a deadline for United Kingdom regulatory approval expires and will immediately move to cut O.I.L. staff and consolidate the companies, he said.
"At the latest, from May 15 to 20, a closing is going to happen," he said at the Offshore Technology Conference here. "The business is going to be consolidated from day one."

Tidewater plans to pay down $200 million to $300 million in debt taken out to finance the O.I.L. deal in about two and a half years and could be out shopping for an acquisition to expand its international business then, he said.
"I don't mind having debt on the balance sheet. I'd be out looking," he told reporters.

O'Malley said recent announcements of new hulls under construction that sank marine services stocks last week would do little to dampen rising rates and revenues during the ongoing offshore drilling boom.
"I thought that was a big over-reaction to a small event," he said, likening the impact of the new hulls on the market to a pre-season loss by a professional basketball team.
